title: CHAPTER TWO. On man's origin specially, and namely on God's existence
english: CHAPTER TWO. On the origin of man specially, where namely of the existence of GOD.

The origin of man has a principle and a mode. We are not treating here of the principle of time in which man began to be, which is the sixth day of the world's creation, but of the principle of production, from which he is and by which he is ruled.

title: I. Man's principle is God; Gen 1:26-27; Acts 17; theology must know God
english: I. The principle of man is God. For man was created by God (Genesis 1:26-27).

But since man is from God and depends on Him above all else in theological reflection place to treat of God. For the theologian cannot lead man back to God his King and principle, and onward to eternal life, unless he has God known.
Hence the Apostle too (Acts 17:24-31) proclaims God the creator; and now commands all everywhere to repent, because He has appointed a day of judgment through Christ raised from the dead.

title: II-V. What can be known of God: sufficiency and efficiency; sufficiency defined
english: II. But God, as He is in Himself, can be known by no one except by Himself (1 Timothy 6:16); yet as He has revealed Himself to us, He is seen as it were from behind (Exodus 33:23), not clearly but enigmatically (1 Corinthians 13:12). But what has been revealed about God suffices for us to live well (Deuteronomy 29:29).
III. Now this which can be known of God is His sufficiency and efficiency. These two are the pillars of faith.

IV. God's sufficiency is that by which He in Himself has enough for Himself and for us: almighty, needing no one and without defect. V. God's sufficiency is considered in His existence, essence, and subsistence.

title: VI. God is, that is, He actually exists; foundation of religion; known in itself vs to us
english: VI. God is, that is, He actually exists. The first and highest foundation and axiom of all true religion is that God is, according to Hebrews 11:6: whoever comes to God must believe that God is.

That God is is indeed known in itself according to nature; yet not according to us, whose knowledge begins from the senses, and therefore we assent only by some prior discourse (Romans 1:20; Acts 17:28; Wisdom 13).
When we speak of God, by the common conception of minds we understand the most perfect being, the first, most powerful, most wise, and best, the producing cause of all things and the governor of all.

title: Against atheists; proof a posteriori by axioms, nature's voice, consensus, conscience
english: Yet it can be demonstrated from the senses against those who deny that God is, such as Diagoras and Epicurus.

Although it is known to every rational creature that God is, and all the pious are persuaded by Scripture and the inward testimony of the Holy Spirit: yet because of the impudence of this age's atheists it must briefly be demonstrated not a priori but a posteriori from effects — by theoretical axioms, by nature's public voice, by the perpetual consensus of all nations, and by the practical axiom which conscience dictates.

title: Reasons 1-4: coordination; first wisdom; first love
english: The first reason is based on the axiom of things' singular existence and coordination. We perceive by sense is from itself. Therefore some one being    necessarily pre-exists from which as first cause all draw origin. But this first being is God.
THE SECOND REASON is founded on the axiom from first wisdom. Every primary efficient cause is more excellent than its effect. Therefore there is one supreme and most wise mind. But this is God.
THE FOURTH REASON is founded on the axiom from first love. All things love to be. This love is not through itself but participated. Therefore there is a first love through itself. But this is God.

title: Reasons 5-8: universe; nature's voice; order; contraries
english: THE FIFTH REASON is founded on the axiom from the universe's existence. The world was not always, because it consists of parts. Therefore it was produced from nothing. But this is God.
THE SIXTH REASON is founded on nature's public voice. Magnitude, multitude, variety, beauty, and perfection cry out that all are from some one. But this is God.
THE SEVENTH REASON is founded on the order of things and their disposition to an end, even of those that lack reason. Every order is from one. But this is God.
THE EIGHTH REASON is founded on the temper and enmity of contraries; a moderator is needed. But this is God.

title: Reasons 9-12: body fabric; stars; harmony; human arts
english: THE NINTH REASON is founded on the body's fabric so skillfully ordered. Only by a most wise craftsman. But this is God.
THE TENTH REASON is founded on contemplation of the stars revolving with marvelous art. But this is God.
THE ELEVENTH REASON is founded on the fatal and necessary harmony of things. But this is God.
THE TWELFTH REASON is founded on the human arts. If man is ruled by art and wisdom, the whole world must be ruled by art and wisdom. And therefore let us believe God.

title: Reasons 13-16: miracles; societies; prophecy; best men's authority
english: THE THIRTEENTH REASON is founded on miracles that exceed the whole force of the created universe. Therefore there is a cause that surpasses the universe. But that is God.
THE FOURTEENTH REASON is founded on the preservation of social, academic, political, and religious institutions, which could not be maintained except by one all-powerful. But that one is God.
THE FIFTEENTH REASON is founded on predictions of future things and their fulfillment (Isaiah 41:22-23).
THE SIXTEENTH REASON is founded on the authority of the best men: Moses, the Prophets, the Apostles, and the better philosophers proved it by miracles, holiness, martyrdom, and prophecy.

title: Reasons 17-18: universal consensus; conscience; against Aristotelian motion — Cap. 2 close
english: THE SEVENTEENTH REASON is founded on the perpetual and universal consensus of all nations and lawgivers. All assert that God is. Whoever denies this consensus will also deny that Rome is and that Caesar was.

THE EIGHTEENTH REASON is founded on the practical axiom which conscience dictates. In all there is a conscience which in good deeds cheers, in evil torments (Romans 2:15; Wisdom 17:11). From which it is gathered that there is a supreme judge. But this is God.

For the rest, whether from motion it can be concluded that God is: those who with Aristotle prove from this labor under a double paralogism. But the reasons by which we have demonstrated that God is can suffice for the present.
